Motto, Vision & Values
Our Motto
Building Bright Futures
Our Vision
Everyone at Red Hill Primary School is committed to providing the building blocks for every child to flourish in a safe and nurturing environment.
We offer a creative curriculum, enriched with opportunities to enable our pupils to understand the world around them and be responsible citizens. Through developing their resilience, independence and confidence, our pupils see learning as a way to realise their full potential.
Our Values
Our motto is Building Bright Futures, and our values – Belonging, Respect, Integrity, Curiosity, Kindness and Strength – spell BRICKS. These are more than words: they are the foundations we lay for every child at Red Hill. BRICKS represent the character we nurture in every classroom and playground; the skills and habits that help children learn, grow and succeed. They also connect us to our place – our school stands on the site of the former Pascall’s Tile and Brick Works – so BRICKS is both a promise and a reminder: the values we teach are the very bricks that build a brighter future for our pupils.
The Pioneer Academy
The Pioneer Academy Vision:
We put children first, pioneering excellence and championing each and every child. Safe – Happy – Learning
The Pioneer Academy Expectations
Schools are safe and secure
Safeguarding is effective and robust
Wellbeing for all
Learners are engaged, resilient and enthusiastic
The Caring Cup
The cup is awarded each week by the teachers, to one child in both Key Stage 1 and 2, who have displayed a particular caring and sympathetic attitude towards their classmates, their work, their teacher or their appearance.
Celebration Assemblies
Celebration assemblies are held each week, and it is at these assemblies that children are presented with the Caring Cup, a P.E., Music or Computing award, a kindness award or being chosen for first place by their class teacher. These are enjoyable assemblies which the children really look forward to because they have the opportunity to share their work or particular success of the week.
Our Red Hill Stars and Red Hill Badges, for Year 6, are presented during achievement assembly by either the Headteacher or Deputy Headteacher on the final week for each half-term. This is a prestigious award given to children for exemplary behaviour and for following the Red Hill Stars.

Head Teacher Welcome
A very warm welcome to Red Hill Primary School
Our motto is ‘Building Bright Futures’. This is in line with our aim of giving our children the skills and experiences to help them become creative, intelligent, resilient, happy and resourceful members of our community. We use the International Primary Curriculum as a foundation for their learning which teaches them about the world they live in whilst developing their social and emotional well-being through personal goals.
Located at the end of Chislehurst High Street, we are proud to be a large part of the local Chislehurst community. We are a primary school, with children joining us in reception (from age 4) and moving on to their secondary school in year six (age 11). We have three classes in each of our Key Stage 1 year groups and, with children joining us from Mead Road Infant School in year 3, we have four classes in each of our Key Stage 2 year groups. Pupils have the benefit of being taught in the familiarity of their own class and year group whilst having access to amazing facilities that is part of the benefit of being a large school. Our facilities include fantastic grounds to support outdoor learning opportunities, active play and sports as well as sports fixtures, iPads and an ICT suite to ensure our pupils have access to up to date technology, a music room, a food technology room, a sensory room, a wild paddock area, two netball courts, a football pitch and even a golf hole!
In September 2016, we became part of The Pioneer Academy, a Multi Academy Trust of primary schools in Bromley, Bexley, Brighton, Hastings, Surrey, Croydon and Kent.
By working with the other schools across the MAT, staff share best practice and have the opportunity to ensure that our pupils are given the very best of opportunities to reach their potential and celebrate their achievements. We work together to ensure that children’s skills and knowledge are built on each year so that by the time they leave year six, they feel confident to embrace all the exciting challenges and opportunities that will be available for them at secondary school.
Please feel free to have a look around our website and get a sense of all the work that we do. We know that education is a partnership between school and home. We strive to build good relationships with all our parents and carers and encourage participation wherever possible.
We look forward to working with you to enable your child to flourish and succeed.

Personal Development
At Red Hill Primary School, we are committed to helping every child grow into a confident, respectful and successful individual. We encourage the development of strong personal values, positive relationships, an appreciation of diversity, and the self-belief needed to achieve their full potential.
Personal development is at the heart of school life and is embedded in everything we do. It is reflected in our daily interactions, classroom learning, assemblies, enrichment activities and educational visits. Our goal is to equip children with the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to thrive beyond the classroom, fostering a sense of belonging, purpose and responsibility as they prepare for the opportunities and challenges of the wider world.
We strive to deliver a meaningful and inspiring curriculum that equips children with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need for the next stage of their education and for life beyond school. We encourage our pupils to aim high, embrace new opportunities and develop a strong understanding of the diverse world around them.
Our curriculum is designed to broaden children's experiences, raise aspirations and help them recognise their own potential. Through our Personal Development provision, pupils gain the knowledge, values and understanding needed to make informed decisions, build positive relationships and contribute positively to their local and wider communities. We are committed to nurturing confident, responsible and respectful individuals who are ready to make a difference in the world.
Children and young people today are growing up in a rapidly changing world where digital technology plays a significant role in their everyday lives. While this brings many exciting opportunities for learning, communication and personal growth, it also presents a range of challenges that they must learn to navigate safely and responsibly.
At Red Hill Primary School, we are committed to helping our pupils develop the knowledge, skills and confidence needed to make informed choices and lead healthy, positive lives. Through our Personal Development curriculum, we foster important qualities such as resilience, self-confidence, independence, effective teamwork, critical thinking and the ability to assess and manage risk. These attributes help prepare children to thrive both in school and in the wider world.

Music
At Red Hill, music is a regular lesson where we use instruments as well as our voices and it is taught in a variety of ways. Music is a subject which uses and improves skills that will be useful in many other subjects; for example, by learning to listen purposefully, working with other people and following directions.
“Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. A high-quality music education should engage and inspire pupils to develop a love of music and their talent as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. As pupils progress, they should develop a critical engagement with music, allowing them to compose, and to listen with discrimination to the best in the musical canon.” National Curriculum (2014).
Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 take part in a weekly singing assembly which will improve both their musicality and their wellbeing. Songs are selected that the children enjoy singing to ensure that they participate fully. Children enjoy singing collectively and sharing familiar, affirmative music.
Most of our music lessons will use the scheme, Sing Up! Lessons are taught either by our specialist music teacher or class teachers.
The key skills we regularly use in music are listening, performing and composing. Children are taught to actively listen and engage with music and to realise the importance of listening to themselves and others. For composition, children start by improvising with other music and develop into creating their own written compositions. Children are encouraged to share what they have done as part of their learning experience. As the children move through the school, they are also taught to use some formal notation – either to read or write their own music. Performance may be of their own composition or of a learnt piece of music. Children are regularly taught songs of different styles, which will also develop their performance or presentation skills.
We have a range of instruments that are used in music lessons. We have a large range of untuned and tuned percussion, including a class set of glockenspiels. We also have class sets of djembes, ukuleles, recorders and keyboards, which are all taught to develop performance skills with our specialist teacher.
We also spend time learning about the styles of music and a little bit about the history of them so that we can use that knowledge in our playing/singing.
At Redhill we run 2 choirs at a time. Our Chamber Choir is for our most confident, KS2 singers, and they regularly perform at school and local events. For the first half of the school year, we also have a Young Voices Choir – which ends in a fabulous performance with professional musicians at the 02 arena. After this has happened, we will also run a “Fun Choir” where all children from year 2 and upwards are invited to have fun singing their favourite songs.
Children are given the opportunity to sing in our 2 choirs. This allows children to further progress with their singing by improving their vocal techniques and learning to sing with a conductor. The children become used to singing in harmony and are given regular opportunities to perform.
Extracurricular Music lessons
We are lucky to have a range of peripatetic instrumental teachers, offering lessons in piano, strings, woodwind and drumming. Rocksteady is also offered to teach singing, keyboard, guitar and bass guitar in a less traditional method.
This year, Year 5 children will be taking part in Band On The Run to learn a new instrument with Bromley Youth Music Trust.

Science
At Red Hill Primary School, we believe that every pupil possesses the curiosity and inquisitiveness of a scientist. Our goal is to instil in our students a genuine passion for and delight in the realm of science. Our commitment extends to fostering their comprehension of vital scientific concepts, processes, and skills while encouraging them to connect these with their day-to-day encounters. We impart diverse modes of thinking, equipping them to enquire effectively and express their thoughts with clarity.
Our aim is to cultivate self-assured, autonomous learners who delve into values and ideas through the lens of science. Our pride lies in the comprehensive and well-rounded approach to teaching science, ensuring every child thrives in the subject throughout their school journey. We firmly believe in every child’s innate scientific inclination, nurturing their curiosity and empowering them to pose questions and independently acquire the skills needed to answer them.
“A high-quality science education provides the foundations for understanding the world through the specific disciplines of biology, chemistry and physics. Science has changed our lives and is vital to the world’s future prosperity, and all pupils should be taught essential aspects of the knowledge, methods, processes and uses of science.” (National Curriculum 2014)
The National Curriculum for Science sets forth key objectives to ensure that every student:
In addition to these national goals, Red Hill is dedicated to:
Red Hill pupils will learn:
Substantive knowledge - subject knowledge and explicit vocabulary linked to their topics.
Disciplinary knowledge – how to collect, use, interpret, understand and evaluate evidence.
At Red Hill, we follow the CUSP curriculum. Our science curriculum is based on the National Curriculum and is designed to help children develop a strong understanding of the world around them. We provide regular opportunities for children to revisit and recall learning.
Science learning begins in the Early Years when children explore the natural world and develop an understanding of people, communities and their environment.
As children move through the school, they build their scientific knowledge, vocabulary and skills. They learn to ask questions, investigate, make observations and think scientifically.
CUSP curriculum is carefully sequenced so that new learning builds on what children already know. This allows pupils to make connections, deepen their understanding and become increasingly confident and knowledgeable young scientists.
Students are fully engrossed in their science subjects, engaging and participating in innovative experiments and honing their enquiry and observation skills. The progression through each year group ensures a cumulative build-up of knowledge, providing students with a profound understanding of each topic.
The core of science lies in planning, recording, predicting, testing, interpreting results, and proposing further investigations. Coupled with practical, hands-on experiences, these elements make science both meaningful and enjoyable for our students. We celebrate science through various events throughout the year, including the annual Science Week, where students dive into diverse areas spanning science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. These events create immersive experiences that captivate students’ interest and curiosity in the fascinating world of science.
In the EYFS, the exploration of science links with the ‘Understanding the World’ part of the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Curriculum. Science is introduced indirectly through activities designed to inspire each child to engage in exploration, problem-solving, observation, prediction, critical thinking, decision-making, and discussions about the world around them.
During their initial years at school, our young learners delve into the areas of creatures, people, plants, and objects within their natural environments. They actively observe and manipulate objects and materials, identifying differences and similarities. Utilising their senses, they might feel dough or listen to sounds in the environment, distinguishing elements like sirens or farm animals. The curriculum encourages them to make observations of animals and plants, providing explanations for occurrences and discussing changes.
Children are prompted to pose questions about the reasons behind events and the workings of things. Engaging activities may involve adjusting the incline of a slope to observe the speed of a vehicle or disassembling a mechanical toy to understand its inner workings. In this process, children are encouraged to predict outcomes, fostering communication, planning, investigation, recording, and the evaluation of their findings. This approach instils a foundation for scientific enquiry and exploration, nurturing curiosity and laying the groundwork for further scientific understanding.

Our Red Hill Curriculum
Inspiring a love of learning
At Red Hill, we want every child to have an extraordinary school day, every day. Our curriculum is designed to spark curiosity, build confidence and give children the knowledge, skills and experiences they need to thrive both in school and beyond.
We believe children learn best when they are actively involved, challenged to think deeply and given opportunities to make meaningful connections between what they already know and what they are learning next.
Our curriculum is ambitious, carefully sequenced and rooted in strong educational research. Alongside developing essential knowledge and skills, we place a strong emphasis on vocabulary, helping children to express themselves confidently and understand the world around them.
We use the Curriculum with Unity Schools Partnership (CUSP) for Reading, Writing, Spelling, Science, History, Geography, Art and Design Technology. CUSP provides a coherent, knowledge-rich curriculum, with carefully planned sequences that build on children's prior learning and reflect the requirements of the National Curriculum.
Each subject is taught as a distinct discipline, helping children to understand its unique knowledge and skills. Where there are meaningful connections between subjects, we make these links explicit so that children can see the bigger picture and apply what they have learnt in different contexts.
Our long-term curriculum plans map out the knowledge and skills children will develop throughout their time at Red Hill. Clear end points help teachers to plan learning carefully, ensuring that new knowledge builds on what has come before and prepares children for what comes next.
We are committed to providing the highest quality teaching across the curriculum. Where specialist expertise can enrich children's learning, we make the most of specialist teachers. Currently, specialist teachers support learning in PE, Computing and Music.
How do children learn?
We use White Rose Mathematics, alongside additional resources, to support the teaching of mathematics. The approach provides a strong foundation in mathematical understanding and promotes mastery, allowing children to develop fluency, reason mathematically and solve problems with confidence.
Reading, Writing and Spelling
CUSP is used for Reading and Writing across the school and for Spelling in Key Stage 2. Its carefully structured approach supports children in developing a rich vocabulary, strong subject knowledge and the ability to communicate effectively.
In the early stages of reading, we use Little Wandle Phonics. Its clear structure, high-quality resources and systematic approach give children the strong foundations they need to become confident, enthusiastic readers.
In EYFS, children learn through a thematic approach which provides exciting, meaningful experiences and opportunities to explore, investigate and develop their understanding of the world.
Our EYFS curriculum is carefully designed to lay the foundations for the knowledge, vocabulary and skills children will build on as they move into Year 1 and throughout their time at Red Hill.
Bringing learning to life
We want learning to be memorable and meaningful. Lessons are carefully planned to be engaging and appropriately challenging, with children encouraged to think, question, discuss, practise and apply their learning.
Our curriculum is designed to build progressively over time. Children regularly revisit important knowledge and skills, strengthening their understanding and making connections with previous learning.
Alongside classroom teaching, we provide a wide range of enrichment opportunities and experiences. These might include practical activities, visits, visitors and opportunities to apply learning in new and exciting ways.
These experiences help children to understand how their learning connects to the wider world and enable them to make links within and across subjects.
How do we know our curriculum is making a difference?
At Red Hill, assessment is an important part of everyday teaching. It helps teachers understand what children know, what they can do and what they need to learn next.
We do not believe assessment should be excessive or onerous. Instead, teachers use a range of approaches throughout lessons to check understanding and respond to children's needs. Questioning, discussion, talk partners, mini whiteboards, quizzes and practical activities all help teachers identify what children have remembered and where further teaching is needed.
Children regularly revisit key knowledge and skills so that important learning becomes embedded in their long-term memory. Summative assessments are also used where appropriate to support teachers in building a clear picture of children's progress and attainment.
Monitoring and evaluating our curriculum
We continually reflect on the quality, impact and relevance of our curriculum. Senior leaders and subject leaders work together to ensure that children experience a broad, ambitious and well-sequenced curriculum.
the coverage, breadth and progression of learning
the quality of children's work in books and online
learning displayed within the school environment
children's views and experiences through pupil voice
assessment information and pupil outcomes
the quality of teaching and learning through learning walks
teacher assessment within individual subjects
This ongoing evaluation helps us identify what is working well and where we can make improvements.
Most importantly, we want children to leave Red Hill as curious, knowledgeable and confident learners who are excited about discovering more.
We want them to remember not just what they have learnt, but the experiences, questions and moments of discovery that made their learning memorable.
At Red Hill, learning is at the heart of all we do. Our curriculum gives every child the opportunity to develop their talents, discover new interests and reach their full potential.

Art, Design and Technology
We are artists and designers.
Art at Red Hill helps learners develop positive attitudes to creative thinking and creative subjects, which benefits future learning. This subject encourages them to celebrate their own and others’ artistic experiences. This builds a sense of community in the classroom from an early age and fosters an openness to diversity as they experience art and design from different times and cultures.
Art at Red Hill gives learners the space to explore and express themselves freely, supporting the development of social and reflective skills, and encouraging teachers to nurture an environment where learners can take risks and build resilience.
We use the CUSP Art Curriculum to provide the children with a rich and carefully planned programme of learning. Lessons are thoughtfully sequenced so that children can build on their knowledge and skills as they progress through school.
Children are introduced to a wide range of artists, designers, craftspeople and artistic traditions. They learn about different styles and cultures whilst developing an understanding of how artists use materials, techniques and ideas to communicate.
Our art curriculum encourages children to:
Art in our sketchbooks
Sketchbooks are an important part of our art learning. They are a place where children can practice their techniques, record ideas, make observations, experiment with materials and develop their artwork.
Design and Technology at Red Hill Primary School
Design and Technology is an innovative and creative subject, with practical learning and problem-solving at the heart of each project. As a subject, it allows children to develop a broad subject knowledge, drawing on their experiences in other subjects. It enables children to learn to take risks, becoming resourceful and enterprising individuals.
“High-quality design and technology education makes an essential contribution to the creativity, culture, wealth and well-being of the nation.” (National Curriculum 2014)
At Red Hill, Design and Technology gives learners the opportunity to explore and express themselves freely. From the moment the design brief is introduced, the children go on a journey through exploration, inventiveness, resilience and reflection. Design Technology is embedded within the IPC topics, where meaningful links to other areas of the curriculum are evident across the school. Following the design process is vital, from research and planning to designing, making and evaluating, all of which equally contribute to the children's successes and achievements. Practical skills are at the centre of this foundation subject, preparing our children for the future.

Computing ​
We are computer scientists.
Welcome to the exciting world of computing at Red Hill Primary School, where innovation and exploration take the spotlight! Our commitment to inspiring young minds is powered by the exceptional ‘Teach Computing’ scheme. Get ready for a thrilling journey into the digital realm that will captivate your child’s imagination and set them on a path to technological excellence.
At Red Hill, we believe in making learning an adventure, and our computing curriculum is no exception. With Teach Computing, we’re not just teaching coding and programming – we’re unleashing creativity, problem-solving prowess, and digital responsibility in every child. Picture your child embarking on a digital quest, equipped with the latest tools and guided by a curriculum designed to spark curiosity and enthusiasm.
“We believe that a high-quality computing education equips pupils to use computational thinking and creativity to understand and change the world.” (National Curriculum 2014)
Discover the computing adventure at Red Hill:
Digital Literacy: Your child will navigate the digital realm with confidence, developing essential skills to evaluate information and thrive in the online world.
Coding and Programming: Prepare for a journey of coding exploration! The Teach Computing framework is our map, guiding your child through interactive and fun activities that unveil the magic of computational thinking.
Online Safety: In the digital landscape, safety is our priority. Teach Computing empowers your child to embrace responsible online behaviour and stay secure in the digital playground.
Embark on a journey of discovery as your child dives into the dynamic world of computing at Red Hill. Our curriculum is designed to ignite a passion for technology through hands-on experiences. Here’s a glimpse of the exciting adventures awaiting your child:
Digital Devices and Software Expedition: Unleash your child’s potential by introducing them to a spectrum of digital tools outlined in the national curriculum. This isn’t just about learning; it’s an expedition to broaden their technological competency.
Problem-Solving: Watch as your child engages in activities that stimulate logical thinking and problem-solving skills, all seamlessly integrated into the Teach Computing framework. It’s not just about finding solutions; it’s about embracing the thrill of the challenge.
Creative Innovation Showcase: Encourage your child to express themselves through digital media, fostering creativity and innovation. Our vast array of resources provide the canvas for their digital masterpieces, setting the stage for imaginative exploration.
Collaboration: In the digital age, teamwork takes centre stage. Teach Computing isn’t just a curriculum; it’s an approach that emphasises the importance of working together. Your child will emerge as a Collaboration Maestro, equipped with essential interpersonal skills.
Early Years Tech Adventure
Even our youngest learners join the excitement! Through playful exploration, Red Hill students in the Early Years identify features of digital devices, building a foundation for a future filled with technological wonder.
At Red Hill Primary School, we take pride in our comprehensive computing curriculum designed to equip students with the essential skills needed to thrive in the digital age. Our curriculum goes beyond the basics, providing a well-rounded and thorough exploration of key areas that are crucial for a child’s success in today’s technologically driven world.

Geography
At Red Hill Primary School, our primary goal is to spark curiosity and enthusiasm about the world, its creation, development, and the profound impact of human actions on its future. Aligned closely with the expectations of the National Curriculum in geography, we strive to cultivate a comprehensive understanding of the world we inhabit. Our aim is to instill in students a heightened awareness of the valuable lessons embedded in past geographical events and human activities, shaping the world as we know it today.
To achieve this, we offer students diverse opportunities to engage with geography through primary and secondary sources, captivating educational visits, and guest speakers seamlessly integrated into our Pioneer Passport program. Geography is intricately woven into our CUSP topics, leveraging our local area and knowledge to breathe life into the thrill of exploration. Students not only absorb geographical concepts but also learn to effectively communicate their knowledge using specialized vocabulary, maps, and honing fieldwork skills. We prioritize creating cross-curricular connections with other subjects to enhance the depth and breadth of their learning experiences.
“A high-quality geography education should inspire in pupils a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people that will remain with them for the rest of their lives.”(National Curriculum 2014)
We implement the CUSP Primary Curriculum to teach geography. The CUSP geography curriculum is an evidence-based, progressive framework designed to build cumulative knowledge and long-lasting memory through structured practice and retrieval.
The curriculum is built around four main conceptual pillars that connect new ideas to prior learning:
In the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), geography skills are taught through knowledge and understanding of the world. They observe, find out about, and identify features in the place they live and the natural world. They find out about their environment, and talk about those features they like and dislike through exploration and investigation.

History
At Red Hill Primary School, we want our pupils to be curious and excited about the past. We help them understand how people, places and societies have changed over time and how the past has shaped the world we live in today.
Through CUSP, pupils explore history using artefacts, photographs, documents, stories, educational visits and other historical sources. They learn to ask questions, make connections between different periods and use evidence to understand the past.
We encourage pupils to develop their historical vocabulary and communicate their ideas clearly. We also make links between history and other subjects to make learning meaningful and memorable.
“A high-quality history education will help pupils gain a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world.” (National Curriculum 2014)
CUSP
We use the CUSP Primary Curriculum to teach history. It is a knowledge-rich curriculum that builds pupils' understanding over time through teaching, retrieval and practice.
CUSP develops pupils' ability to think like historians:
Pupils also develop their understanding of important historical concepts such as power, invasion, community, monarchy, society, empire and democracy.

Mathematics
We are mathematicians.
At Red Hill Primary School, our aim is to foster the growth of self-motivated, confident learners among our students. We focus on equipping them with the skills to use and apply mathematics effectively in various situations. Our math curriculum is designed to instill a sense of curiosity, enjoyment, and passion for the subject, recognizing its unique power to help children make sense of and describe the world around them. Additionally, it empowers them to tackle and solve problems with mathematical insight.
“A high-quality mathematics education provides a foundation for understanding the world, theability to reason mathematically, an appreciation of the beauty and power of mathematics, and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject.” (National Curriculum 2014)
Red Hill mathematicians
As mathematicians, we are adept thinkers and skilled problem solvers. Leveraging our existing mathematical knowledge, we establish connections across various mathematical domains, facilitating effective reasoning. Our approach involves utilizing diverse manipulatives, resources, and diagrams to articulate and enhance our comprehension of mathematical concepts.
In alignment with the full National Curriculum, we implement the White Rose Mathematics update scheme throughout the school. This scheme is designed to support all students in mastering mathematics. To complement this, we incorporate resources from Classroom Secrets and Deepening Understanding into our teaching practices.
What does it mean to master mathematics?
A pupil has truly mastered a mathematical concept or skill when they can represent it in various ways, possess the necessary mathematical language to articulate related ideas, and can independently apply the concept to solve new problems in unfamiliar situations.
Mastery is a continuous journey and a long-term goal that involves exploration, clarification, practice, and application over time. At each stage of learning, pupils are expected to showcase a profound, conceptual understanding of the topic, with the ability to build upon it as they progress.
The emphasis is not solely on memorizing key facts and procedures, as this often leads to a superficial understanding that can be easily forgotten. Instead, pupils should have the capacity to discern the most effective mathematical approach for different scenarios, showcasing a more comprehensive and adaptable understanding of the subject matter.
All pupils can achieve in mathematics
The development of mathematical abilities is a result of consistent practice, dedicated support, and hard work rather than relying solely on natural talent, which is just an initial advantage and does not determine one’s potential for achievement.
For high-attaining pupils, a deep understanding of key number concepts is emphasized over mere memorization of processes. Teachers aim to extend the learning experience for high-achieving students by delving into the depth of concepts rather than accelerating them into new content prematurely. This approach ensures a more thorough and comprehensive mastery of mathematical principles.
It is essential to enhance comprehension before progressing to material from the next academic level. Deepening understanding of mathematical concepts proves beneficial for all students, irrespective of previous struggles or successes. Providing students with adequate time to thoroughly grasp, explore, and apply ideas is crucial. This method ensures a genuine understanding of a concept, and the challenge lies in investigating it through new, alternative, and more complex approaches.
Multiple representations for all
The White Rose approach embraces the ubiquity of objects, pictures, words, numbers, and symbols in our surroundings. By incorporating all these elements, it aids students in exploring and expressing mathematical ideas, thereby enhancing their learning experience and fostering a deeper understanding. The synergy of these components contributes to solidifying knowledge, ensuring that students truly comprehend what they’ve learned.
Concrete:Students are encouraged to use tangible objects and manipulatives, such as cubes, to gain a hands-on understanding and articulate their actions.
Pictorial: Building on the concrete foundation, students progress to using pictorial representations. These visuals serve as tools for reasoning and problem-solving.
Abstract: With a well-established foundation, students can confidently transition to an abstract approach, employing numbers and key concepts to further advance their understanding.
Fluency, reasoning and problem solving
Fluency refers to a student’s ability to efficiently and accurately apply mathematical procedures and concepts. It involves being able to perform basic arithmetic operations, such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, with ease and speed. Fluency extends beyond mere memorisation of facts; it includes a deep understanding of number relationships and the ability to use that understanding to solve problems quickly and accurately.
Our approach places mathematical problem-solving at its core. We inspire students to identify, comprehend, and apply pertinent mathematical principles, fostering connections between various ideas. This process cultivates the skills required to address novel problems, moving beyond mere repetition of routines without a solid understanding.
To provide a more comprehensive and profound learning experience, we explore mathematical concepts through diverse representations and within various problem-solving contexts. This approach allows students to integrate different concepts, enabling them to solve intricate problems and apply their knowledge to real-life situations.
The transformation of students’ learning in mathematics is significantly influenced by how they articulate their understanding. Mastery-oriented methodologies, exemplified by approaches like White Rose, employ a meticulously sequenced and structured method to introduce and bolster mathematical vocabulary. Students are encouraged to articulate their mathematical thoughts in complete sentences, going beyond merely stating the answer to explaining the rationale behind it. This emphasis is critical for cultivating both mathematical language and reasoning skills.
Maths across the curriculum
While the mathematics curriculum is typically organized as a distinct subject, there exists a wealth of potential for cross-curricular activities. Establishing connections between different areas of learning enriches children’s understanding by offering opportunities to reinforce and enhance their learning. The enhancement of learning is achieved through several strategies:
Under the new maths curriculum (2014) the expectation is “By the end of year 6, pupils should be fluent in written methods for all 4 operations, including long multiplication and division, and in working with fractions, decimals and percentages.” Our calculation Policy, which has been written in line with the programmes of study taken from the revised National Curriculum for Mathematics (2014) provides guidance on appropriate calculation methods and progression. The content is set out in yearly blocks under the following headings: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. Statements taken directly from the programmes of study are listed in bold at the beginning of each section.
Mastering times tables is a fundamental aspect of your child’s mathematical education. Proficiency in times tables provides a strong foundation in mathematics, benefiting them as they progress within the subject. While many children can recite their times tables in order, independently knowing the answer to any times table question is a skill that requires substantial effort and dedication. The national expectations for times tables by year group are outlined as follows:
By the end of Key Stage 2 (KS2), it is expected that children have a secure understanding of their times tables, enabling them to answer any times table question mentally within a five-second timeframe. This proficiency is crucial for their continued success in mathematics.

Modern Foreign Languages
At Red Hill Primary School, French is taught using resources from the online system Language Angels. The scheme of work shows progression across the four years of KS2. It aligns well with the five key strands set out in the KS2 Languages Framework – Oracy, Literacy, Intercultural Understanding, Knowledge About Languages and Language Learning Strategies.
Learning a foreign language is a liberation from insularity and provides an opening to other cultures. A high-quality languages education should foster pupils’ curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world. (National Curriculum, 2014).
The scheme of work allows children to develop their sense of belonging to the wider world, express ideas and thoughts in another language and understand and respond to French speakers. We challenge children to express their ideas and thoughts in another language, and to understand and respond to its speakers, which is essential, practical knowledge for all global citizens.
Through the use of games, flashcards and songs, we engage children to develop specific knowledge of French, learning words and structures that enable them to ask and answer questions, listen to, read and understand stories, songs, poems and other short texts, and to write from memory.
I – Inspire children to develop a sense of belonging to the wider World.
C – Challenge children to express their ideas and thoughts in another language, and to understand and respond to its speakers, which is essential, practical knowledge for all global citizens.
E – Engage through the use of flashcards, games and songs to develop specific knowledge of French, learning words and structures that enable them to ask and answer questions.
In French lessons, we inspire children to develop their sense of belonging to the wider world and embark on a journey towards a wealth of opportunities in their future lives. We provide opportunities to explore the relationship between language and identity, develop an international outlook and grow into an enhanced understanding of the world and their place within it.
